subject: zoology
question_text: What are the functions of the canal system of sponges?

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack zoology section (book p.53, VSAQ 89). Zoology holds only ONE source book — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no zoology board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

steps.label: The water current
steps.why: Every function of the canal system is carried out by the one water current that runs through it, so the path of the water is written first.
common_mistakes: Writing that the water leaves through the ostia. Water enters by the ostia and leaves by the osculum.
Calling the canal system a digestive system. It is a water current system.
steps.memory_tip: One current, three jobs: in through the ostia, out through the osculum.
steps.margin_note: Name the parts of the water path first. Three short lines.

steps.label: The three functions
steps.why: One current does three different things depending on what is taken from it or added to it, which is why a single structure answers three functions.
common_mistakes: Giving only one function. The question asks for the functions, so name all three.
Writing that the sponge pumps water with muscles. The flagella of the choanocytes drive the current.
steps.memory_tip: Food in, gases exchanged, waste out — all on the same stream of water.
steps.margin_note: Three numbered functions, one line each. Name the process beside each one.
lines: 1) Nutrition: the current brings in food
particles, which the choanocytes take up.
2) Respiration: oxygen dissolved in the water
is taken up and carbon dioxide is given out.
The same current also carries out the sperms
and the larvae at the breeding season.

insider_note: Two marks for three functions, so the examiner is ticking the words nutrition, respiration and excretion — write all three even if the third takes only four words.
